cards.name: Scyther
cards.description: The sharp scythes on its forearms become increasingly sharp by cutting through hard objects.

cards.name: Pineco
cards.description: It spits out a fluid that it uses to glue tree bark to its body. The fluid hardens when it touches air.

cards.name: Seedot
cards.description: If it remains still, it looks just like a real nut. It delights in surprising foraging Pokémon.

cards.name: Nuzleaf
cards.description: It lives deep in forests. With the leaf on its head, it makes a flute whose song makes listeners uneasy.

cards.name: Shiftry
cards.description: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe's mind and take preemptive action.

cards.name: Shroomish
cards.description: If it senses danger, it scatters spores from the top of its head to protect itself.

cards.name: Breloom
cards.description: The seeds on its tail are made of toxic spores. It knocks out foes with quick, virtually invisible punches.

cards.name: Roselia
cards.description: Its flowers give off a relaxing fragrance. The stronger its aroma, the healthier the Roselia is.

cards.name: Roserade
cards.description: After captivating opponents with its sweet scent, it lashes them with its thorny whips.

cards.name: Turtwig
cards.description: Photosynthesis occurs across its body under the sun. The shell on its back is actually hardened soil.

cards.name: Grotle
cards.description: It lives along water in forests. In the daytime, it leaves the forest to sunbathe its treed shell.

cards.name: Shaymin
cards.description: It can dissolve toxins in the air to instantly transform ruined land into a lush field of flowers.

cards.name: Cottonee
cards.description: It shoots cotton from its body to protect itself. If it gets caught up in hurricane-strength winds, it can get sent to the other side of the Earth.

cards.name: Whimsicott
cards.description: It scatters cotton all over the place as a prank. If it gets wet, it'll become too heavy to move and have no choice but to answer for its mischief.

cards.name: Deerling
cards.description: Deerling have different scents depending on the season. In this form, Deerling have a softly sweet scent that lingers in the nose.

cards.name: Sawsbuck
cards.description: Sawsbuck in their Autumn Form are known for having very short tempers. The males fight each other incessantly.

cards.name: Grubbin
cards.description: Its natural enemies, like Rookidee, may flee rather than risk getting caught in its large mandibles that can snap thick tree branches.

cards.name: Dhelmise
cards.description: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.

cards.name: Bramblin
cards.description: Not even Bramblin knows where it is headed as it tumbles across the wilderness, blown by the wind. It loathes getting wet.

cards.name: Brambleghast
cards.description: Brambleghast wanders around arid regions. On rare occasions, mass outbreaks of these Pokémon will bury an entire town.

cards.name: Rellor
cards.description: It rolls its mud ball around while the energy it needs for evolution matures. Eventually the time comes for it to evolve.

cards.name: Rabsca
cards.description: An infant sleeps inside the ball. Rabsca rolls the ball soothingly with its legs to ensure the infant sleeps comfortably.

cards.name: Ponyta
cards.description: It can't run properly when it's newly born. As it races around with others of its kind, its legs grow stronger.

cards.name: Rapidash
cards.description: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.

cards.name: Slugma
cards.description: A common sight in volcanic areas, it slowly slithers around in a constant search for warm places.

cards.name: Magcargo
cards.description: Its brittle shell occasionally spouts intense flames that circulate throughout its body.

cards.name: Victini
cards.description: This Pokémon brings victory. It is said that Trainers with Victini always win, regardless of the type of encounter.

cards.name: Heatmor
cards.description: There's a hole in its tail that allows it to draw in the air it needs to keep its fire burning. If the hole gets blocked, this Pokémon will fall ill.

cards.name: Litten
cards.description: It spends even the smallest amount of downtime grooming its fur with its tongue. Loose fur gathers in its stomach and serves as fuel for fiery moves.

cards.name: Torracat
cards.description: In the midst of battle, the fire pouch on Torracat's neck rings like a bell and produces stronger flames than usual.

cards.name: Turtonator
cards.description: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.

cards.name: Sizzlipede
cards.description: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.

cards.name: Centiskorch
cards.description: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.

cards.name: Totodile
cards.description: It is small but rough and tough. It won't hesitate to take a bite out of anything that moves.

cards.name: Croconaw
cards.description: If it loses a fang, a new one grows back in its place. There are always 48 fangs lining its mouth.

cards.name: Feraligatr
cards.description: It usually moves slowly, but it goes at blinding speed when it attacks and bites prey.

cards.name: Carvanha
cards.description: It won't attack while it's alone—not even if it spots prey. Instead, it waits for other Carvanha to join it, and then the Pokémon attack as a group.

cards.name: Sharpedo
cards.description: As soon as it catches the scent of prey, Sharpedo will jet seawater from its backside, hurtling toward the target to attack at 75 mph.

cards.name: Keldeo
cards.description: Keldeo has strengthened its resolve for battle, filling its body with power and changing its form.

cards.name: Snom
cards.description: It eats snow that has accumulated on the ground. It prefers soft, freshly fallen snow, so it will eat its way up a mountain, aiming for the peak.

cards.name: Frosmoth
cards.description: Frosmoth senses air currents with its antennae. It sends its scales drifting on frigid air, making them fall like snow.

cards.name: Wiglett
cards.description: This Pokémon can pick up the scent of a Veluza just over 65 feet away and will hide itself in the sand.

cards.name: Finizen
cards.description: It likes playing with others of its kind using the water ring on its tail. It uses ultrasonic waves to sense the emotions of other living creatures.

cards.name: Palafin
cards.description: This Pokémon's ancient genes have awakened. It is now so extraordinarily strong that it can easily lift a cruise ship with one fin.

cards.name: Pikachu
cards.description: When several of these Pokémon gather, their electricity can build and cause lightning storms.

cards.name: Raichu
cards.description: If the electric pouches in its cheeks become fully charged, both ears will stand straight up.

cards.name: Electabuzz
cards.description: Many power plants keep Ground-type Pokémon around as a defense against Electabuzz that come seeking electricity.

cards.name: Electivire
cards.description: The amount of electrical energy this Pokémon produces is proportional to the rate of its pulse. The voltage jumps while Electivire is battling.

cards.name: Charjabug
cards.description: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.

cards.name: Vikavolt
cards.description: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.

cards.name: Zeraora
cards.description: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.

cards.name: Yamper
cards.description: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.

cards.name: Boltund
cards.description: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.

cards.name: Iron Hands
cards.description: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

cards.name: Iron Thorns
cards.description: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

cards.name: Mr. Mime
cards.description: The broadness of its hands may be no coincidence—many scientists believe its palms became enlarged specifically for pantomiming.

cards.name: Marill
cards.description: The fur on its body naturally repels water. It can stay dry even when it plays in the water.

cards.name: Azumarill
cards.description: Its long ears are superb sensors. It can distinguish the movements of things in water and tell what they are.

cards.name: Girafarig
cards.description: Girafarig's tail has a small head. It instinctively bites at any foe that approaches the Pokémon from behind.

cards.name: Latias
cards.description: It communicates using telepathy. Its body is covered in down that refracts light to make it invisible.

cards.name: Bronzor
cards.description: Ancient people believed that the pattern on Bronzor's back contained a mysterious power.

cards.name: Bronzong
cards.description: In ages past, this Pokémon was revered as a bringer of rain. It was found buried in the ground.

cards.name: Solosis
cards.description: It communicates with others telepathically. Its body is encapsulated in liquid, but if it takes a heavy blow, the liquid will leak out.

cards.name: Duosion
cards.description: Its psychic power can supposedly cover a range of more than half a mile—but only if its two brains can agree with each other.

cards.name: Reuniclus
cards.description: While it could use its psychic abilities in battle, this Pokémon prefers to swing its powerful arms around to beat opponents into submission.

cards.name: Elgyem
cards.description: If this Pokémon stands near a TV, strange scenery will appear on the screen. That scenery is said to be from its home.

cards.name: Beheeyem
cards.description: Whenever a Beheeyem visits a farm, a Dubwool mysteriously disappears.

cards.name: Cutiefly
cards.description: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur's pollen.

cards.name: Ribombee
cards.description: It makes pollen puffs from pollen and nectar. The puffs' effects depend on the type of ingredients and how much of each one is used.

cards.name: Scream Tail
cards.description: There has been only one reported sighting of this Pokémon. It resembles a mysterious creature depicted in an old expedition journal.

cards.name: Flutter Mane
cards.description: This Pokémon has characteristics similar to those of Flutter Mane, a creature mentioned in a certain book.

cards.name: Iron Valiant
cards.description: It's possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

cards.name: Iron Valiant
cards.description: It's possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

cards.name: Meditite
cards.description: It meditates to heighten its inner energy and to float in the air. It eats one berry a day.

cards.name: Medicham
cards.description: It elegantly avoids attacks with dance-like steps, then launches a devastating blow in the same motion.

cards.name: Relicanth
cards.description: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.

cards.name: Drilbur
cards.description: It brings its claws together and whirls around at high speed before rushing toward its prey.

cards.name: Excadrill
cards.description: It's not uncommon for tunnels that appear to have formed naturally to actually be a result of Excadrill's rampant digging.

cards.name: Golett
cards.description: They were sculpted from clay in ancient times. No one knows why, but some of them are driven to continually line up boulders.

cards.name: Golurk
cards.description: Artillery platforms built into the walls of ancient castles served as perches from which Golurk could fire energy beams.

cards.name: Rockruff
cards.description: This Pokémon is very friendly when it's young. Its disposition becomes vicious once it matures, but it never forgets the kindness of its master.

cards.name: Lycanroc
cards.description: Lycanroc attacks its prey with its sharp claws and fangs. It loyally obeys the instructions of a Trainer it trusts.

cards.name: Mudbray
cards.description: This Pokémon covers itself in mud that it has regurgitated. The mud won't dry out even if it's exposed to the sun for a long time.

cards.name: Mudsdale
cards.description: This Pokémon has been treasured not just for its physical labor but also because it produces high-quality mud used for making pottery.

cards.name: Rolycoly
cards.description: On sunny days, Rolycoly will come out onto grassy plains and roll around. Then it will eat the grass that gets tangled in its wheel-like leg.

cards.name: Carkol
cards.description: The temperature inside its body increases when it experiences strong emotions. It rolls around frantically while spewing flames.

cards.name: Coalossal
cards.description: To intimidate its opponents, Coalossal will vigorously shake its body, scattering coal from its smoldering back.

cards.name: Great Tusk
cards.description: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

cards.name: Great Tusk
cards.description: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. The name Great Tusk was taken from a creature listed in a certain book.

cards.name: Sandy Shocks
cards.description: No records exist of this Pokémon being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon's traits match up with a creature shown in an expedition journal.

cards.name: Ekans
cards.description: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.

cards.name: Arbok
cards.description: The pattern on its belly appears to be a frightening face. Weak foes will flee just at the sight of the pattern.

cards.name: Gastly
cards.description: It wraps its opponent in its gas-like body, slowly weakening its prey by poisoning it through the skin.

cards.name: Haunter
cards.description: It likes to lurk in the dark and tap shoulders with a gaseous hand. Its touch causes endless shuddering.

cards.name: Poochyena
cards.description: A Pokémon with a persistent nature, it chases its chosen prey until the prey becomes exhausted.

cards.name: Mightyena
cards.description: It will always obey the commands of a skilled Trainer. Its behavior arises from its living in packs in ancient times.

cards.name: Sableye
cards.description: It dwells in the darkness of caves. It uses its sharp claws to dig up gems to nourish itself.

cards.name: Roaring Moon
cards.description: It is possible that this is the creature listed as Roaring Moon in an expedition journal that still holds many mysteries.

cards.name: Forretress
cards.description: Its entire body is shielded by a steel-hard shell. What lurks inside this shell is a total mystery.

cards.name: Mawile
cards.description: It uses its docile-looking face to lull foes into complacency, then bites with its huge, relentless jaws.

cards.name: Beldum
cards.description: From its rear, Beldum emits a magnetic force that rapidly pulls opponents in. They get skewered on Beldum's sharp claws.

cards.name: Metang
cards.description: Two Beldum have become stuck together via their own magnetic forces. With two brains, the resulting Metang has doubled psychic powers.

cards.name: Metagross
cards.description: Because the magnetic powers of these Pokémon get stronger in freezing temperatures, Metagross living on snowy mountains are full of energy.

cards.name: Meltan
cards.description: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.

cards.name: Melmetal
cards.description: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.

cards.name: Iron Treads
cards.description: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

cards.name: Koraidon
cards.description: This seems to be the Winged King mentioned in an old expedition journal. It was said to have split the land with its bare fists.

cards.name: Miraidon
cards.description: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

cards.name: Lickitung
cards.description: If this Pokémon's sticky saliva gets on you and you don't clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won't go away, either.

cards.name: Lickilicky
cards.description: Lickilicky's strange tongue can stretch to many times the length of its body. No one has figured out how Lickilicky's tongue can stretch so far.

cards.name: Hoothoot
cards.description: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.

cards.name: Noctowl
cards.description: Its eyes are specially developed to enable it to see clearly even in murky darkness and minimal light.

cards.name: Dunsparce
cards.description: It creates mazes in dark locations. When spotted, it flees into the ground by digging with its tail.

cards.name: Dudunsparce
cards.description: This Pokémon uses its hard tail to make its nest by boring holes into bedrock deep underground. The nest can reach lengths of over six miles.

cards.name: Skitty
cards.description: It can't stop itself from chasing moving things, and it runs in a circle, chasing its own tail.

cards.name: Delcatty
cards.description: It dislikes dirty places. It often searches for a comfortable place in which to groom itself.

cards.name: Chatot
cards.description: It mimics the cries of other Pokémon to trick them into thinking it's one of them. This way they won't attack it.

cards.name: Pidove
cards.description: Where people go, these Pokémon follow. If you're scattering food for them, be careful— several hundred of them can gather at once.

cards.name: Tranquill
cards.description: It can fly moderately quickly. No matter how far it travels, it can always find its way back to its master and its nest.

cards.name: Unfezant
cards.description: Unfezant are exceptional fliers. The females are known for their stamina, while the males outclass them in terms of speed.

cards.name: Minccino
cards.description: The way it brushes away grime with its tail can be helpful when cleaning. But its focus on spotlessness can make cleaning more of a hassle.

cards.name: Cinccino
cards.description: Its body secretes oil that this Pokémon spreads over its nest as a coating to protect it from dust. Cinccino won't tolerate even a speck of the stuff.

cards.name: Drampa
cards.description: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.

cards.name: Iron Jugulis
cards.description: It's possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

cards.name: Shiftry
cards.description: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe's mind and take preemptive action.

cards.name: Grotle
cards.description: It lives along water in forests. In the daytime, it leaves the forest to sunbathe its treed shell.
